contract_deviations: Architecture section 2.3 shows the backfill as UPDATE ... SET ym = to_char(run_date, 'YYYY-MM') WHERE ym IS NULL. This T-01B uses a CASE expression so synthetic rows get the SYN-002A sentinel (which section 2.3 also names), and so a row with NULL run_date but non-null started_at still gets a valid ym (to_char(started_at, 'YYYY-MM')). The final UNKNOWN fallback exists only to make the backfill defensive against malformed legacy rows; there are 0 such rows at migration time. This is a tightening of the contract, not a deviation.

Architecture section 2.3 shows duplicate-collapse via 'DELETE p1 USING p2 WHERE p1.run_id < p2.run_id AND (ym, source, method, noise) tuple match'. This T-01B uses the ROW_NUMBER() window pattern instead. Equivalent set-theoretic result (both keep max(run_id) per group); window pattern is O(n log n) instead of O(n^2) and is friendlier to large tables. Same final row shape.
notes: The 77-row duplicate-collapse is dominated by (SYN-002A, synthetic, *, *) groups with 5-14 rows each from prior matrix sweeps (expected under WI-1 workflow where a cell could be rerun without a constraint). The 2026-11 real-source duplicates are 12 zenodo time_gap/N0 + 3 s3 kinematic*/N0 groups of 2 - consistent with scrape re-runs during the CONDITIONAL_ACCEPTANCE phase. Post-migration row count (25) matches the architecture-spec cardinality of 25 distinct (ym, source, method, noise) tuples across the recorded sources.
